main_text.p: platonem & Ariftotelem traduxisse, à Io-sepho ubi contra Apionem, & Cyrillo ubi contra Iulianum agit, varijs ethnico-rum testimonijs probatur. Sed ita hoc ab ijs factum, ut rivos ex puris his fon-tibus, ad philosophiam derivatos, adeò ineptis suis figmentis & lutulentis ratio-nibus infecerint, nihil ut omnis doctri-na illorum, de cœlestibus mysterijs, nisi errorem doceat, mentemque à syncerítate fidei & cultus divini avocet. Limites enim suos egressum ingenium illorum, postquam se rebus divinis immersit, relicto sacræ scri-pturæ gubernaculo, nihil nisi errorem, eò magis nocuum quo speciosiorem parere potuit. Quocirca ne lumen quod in nobis esse debet tenebræ sint, illud animo fixum hæreat, respuendam illam esse philoso-phiam ex Apostoli præcepto, tanquam pellicem quæ nos ad adulterium invitat, dum ex elementis mundanæ sapientiæ, effectis ad sacrorum scripturarum imita-tionem, quibusam veræ pietatis simu-lachris, summi boni fruitionem & vitam beatam, funesto cum dolo, præcepto-rum suorum observatoribus pollicetur, profiteturque se magistram quæ ad immor-talitatem ducat. Longè alia hæc fuit Philosophia, ab illa quam nos hodie in scholis

page.notes: Left margin: reference mark "Col. 2. s" beside the first lines of the paragraph opposite the line "phiam ex Apostoli" — printed as a small marginal reference; transcribed as a note in the text position it stands beside. Marginal marks: small mark (asterisk-like) beside "beatam," in the right side of the printed line, shown in the scan as a reference sign; not a word. Bottom of the text: "scholis" is a line-ending word at the foot of the column (not a catchword in the strict sense, since it continues the sentence); the wording "fcholis" in the bottom_margin should be read as "scholis" with long s; the page's last word has been kept in the text. Some words in the lower right area are faint; readings are as printed to the best of legibility.
